extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and policymakers / delegates to the United Nations Food Conference
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted principles and standards discussed at the first United Nations conference on post-war food and agriculture (statements by President Roosevelt, Judge Marvin Jones and others). These are high-level policy criteria for producing and managing post-war food production, distribution, conservation and related international arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop world food production adequate to meet essential nutritional needs
rubrics_metrics.description: “They must take all necessary steps to develop world food production so that it will be adequate to meet the essential nutritional needs of the world population.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roosevelt: each nation individually and all nations collectively must undertake responsibilities to expand production; this is a long-term program though temporary measures may be needed in the interim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove hindrances to food access (trade, transportation, internal distribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: “They must see to it that no hindrances, whether of international trade, of transportation or of internal distribution, be allowed to prevent any nation or group of citizens within a nation from obtaining the food necessary for health.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on eliminating barriers at international and domestic levels that block access to food; includes trade policy, transport infrastructure and internal market/distribution impediments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarantee minimum adequate nutrition for all members of society
rubrics_metrics.description: “Society must meet in full its obligation to make available to all its members at least the minimum adequate nutrition.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as a societal obligation tied to health and the Four Freedoms; an explicit universal minimum-nutrition objective for post-war policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve global distribution channels so surpluses reach needy markets
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote the flow of farm commodities and the articles produced thereinto the markets of the world; make it possible for surplus products to be distributed and used and thus prevent them from overloading and overwhelming the distribution machinery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference aim to address clogged channels of commerce, open new channels and outlets so that bursting barns and rotting surpluses do not coexist with hunger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address surpluses caused by distribution and purchasing-power failures
rubrics_metrics.description: “What we have called surpluses are for the most part not surpluses at all, but are the results of accumulations caused by defects in the systems of distribution and the inability of the masses to purchase the food they need.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy must tackle both distribution system defects and insufficient consumer purchasing power rather than treating surpluses purely as overproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stabilize prices and protect producers from ruinously low prices
rubrics_metrics.description: “Wasting surpluses frequently cause ruinously low prices to the producer... The consequent extreme fluctuations in price are to the advantage of neither the producer nor the consumer. Stored reserves, a fair price...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measures such as stored reserves and fair pricing mechanisms to reduce price volatility and ensure both producer and consumer welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate freer flow of commodities in world trade to enable specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: “The freer flow of commodities in world trade will enable each nation to produce what it is best equipped and suited to produce.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument for freer international trade in agricultural commodities so nations can specialize according to comparative advantage; linked to opening markets and outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use temporary devices for immediate needs while pursuing long-range programs
rubrics_metrics.description: “In the mean time, it may be necessary for the nations to deal on a temporary basis with... long-range objective of fully utilizing the products of human skill and energy.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts short-term, temporary measures to deal with post-war emergencies while keeping sight of long-term structural programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conserve and rebuild natural resources (soil, timber, minerals); combat erosion
rubrics_metrics.description: “Every nation should become vitally interested in the conservation of natural resources, soil, timber and minerals and the rebuilding of them where they have been depleted and are being wasted... It is estimated that at least one-third of the tilled land of the earth has been seriously affected by erosion.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy priorities include soil-building, erosion control, water management and reforestation; exchange of methods is encouraged to improve national practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange agricultural knowledge and technical advice internationally
rubrics_metrics.description: “They need the advice and suggestion of those peoples who have had longer experience in these vital problems. We hope that an exchange of ideas will be mutually helpful.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages sharing of methods, practices and technical experience among nations and adapting practices to local economies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect national sovereignty in implementing measures
rubrics_metrics.description: “Each nation must be the final judge of what is best suited to its conditions.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International cooperation should allow nations discretion to choose methods appropriate to their own economic, social and ecological conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote mutual assistance that builds capacity rather than charity
rubrics_metrics.description: “What humanity wants is not charity but a free opportunity, the chance to work and help to build.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on enabling production and self-sufficiency (training, access, markets) rather than one-way charitable transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert wartime production and materials to constructive peacetime uses
rubrics_metrics.description: “The same materials go into the sewing machine that go into the machine gun... What achieves progress should be geared to the mind and heart.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repurpose industrial capacity and materials from destructive to productive civilian uses (e.g., convert plants and materials to peacetime goods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use food distribution as an instrument to help maintain peace
rubrics_metrics.description: “Food is a powerful weapon of warfare. Food may be even more effective in helping to maintain peace.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure equitable food availability post-war to prevent hunger-driven instability and to support peace-building objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-war international aviation principles (reciprocity, shortest routes, supervision not ownership)
rubrics_metrics.description: Airlines proposed immediate reciprocal exchange of the general right of innocent flight with the right to land for refueling and other technical purposes; that airlines should have the shortest possible air routes to all countries of recognized or potential commercial importance; vigorous opposition to government management or ownership but acceptance of government supervision and some international regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carriers recommended reciprocal landing/refueling rights, preparation for conversion to peacetime production, government supervision for safety/rules-of-the-road, and resistance to nationalized airline ownership.
